newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet approves zero coupon bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet approves zero coupon bond issue.

text.p: Thailand's cabinet on Tuesday approved the issue of 50 billion baht in zero coupon bonds to raise funds to help cash-strapped firms in the depressed property and financial sectors, a central bank official said.

The first tranche of bonds to be auctioned from the total amount approved by the cabinet would take place on Friday (May 2), assistant Bank of Thailand governor Siri Ganjarerndee told reporters after the cabinet meeting.
The amount of bonds to be auctioned would be decided on later by a committee that would take into account liquidity conditions in the local financial system before agreeing on a value, he added.

The bond issue is part of a rescue scheme under which the government plans to issue up to 100 billion baht of bonds to bail out the depressed property and financial sector which have been hit by liquidity woes.
The bonds will carry a seven-year maturity and would qualify to be a part of commercial banks and finance companies reserve requirements.

Proceeds from the auction would be managed by the recently-established government-run Property Loans Management Organization to purchase non-performing property loans from banks and finance companies.
Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday that if the initial 50 billion baht was not enough, the government would issue another 50 billion baht.
Each tranche of bonds issued would not exceed 10 billion baht as the government would like to keep liquidity at appropriate levels, he added.
